\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Reachability in a directed graph]
\lean{Complexity.GraphReach}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p035-b005}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p012-b002,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p012-b003
}
\label{Complexity.GraphReach}
\leanok
For a natural number $n$, a Boolean adjacency function $A$ on ordered pairs of vertices
in $\\{0,\\ldots,n-1\\}$, and vertices $s$ and $t$, define $t$ to be reachable from $s$
when there is a finite directed walk from $s$ to $t$ whose every step $u\\to v$
satisfies $A(u,v)=\\mathrm{true}$. Walks of length zero are allowed.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Encoding a directed path instance]
\lean{Complexity.encodePATH}
\statementsource{Sav70}{pdf-c8033d2fd705-p012-b004}
\label{Complexity.encodePATH}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $A$ be a Boolean matrix indexed by pairs of vertices in
$brange{0,n}$, and let $s,t$ be vertices among these $n$ vertices. Encode the data by
pairing the length-$n$ list consisting entirely of true values with a pairing of the
row-by-row list of entries of $A$ and a pairing of the binary expansions of $s$ and $t$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Directed reachability language]
\lean{Complexity.PATH}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p035-b005}
\statementsource{Sav70}{
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p012-b003,
  pdf-c8033d2fd705-p012-b005
}
\label{Complexity.PATH}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.GraphReach, Complexity.encodePATH}
Let $\mathrm{PATH}$ be the language of Boolean strings that are the encoding of some
directed graph on $n$ vertices together with two vertices $s,t$, for some natural number
$n$, where $t$ is reachable from $s$ in that graph by a finite directed walk, possibly
of length zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Length of the adjacency word]
\lean{Complexity.length_adjWord}
\label{Complexity.length_adjWord}
\leanok
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $A$ assign a Boolean value to each ordered pair of
elements of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. The list formed by concatenating, for each first
coordinate in increasing order, the list of values of $A$ over all second coordinates in
increasing order has length $n^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Indexing rows in a flat map]
\lean{Complexity.getD_flatMap_rows}
\label{Complexity.getD_flatMap_rows}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $L$ be a finite list over a type $\alpha$, let $f$ map each element to a Boolean
list, and suppose every list $f(a)$ has length $k$. For $i<|L|$ and $j<k$, the element
at index $ik+j$ of the concatenation of the lists $f(a)$ for $a$ in $L$, using false as
the default when out of range, equals the element at index $j$ of $f(L_i)$ with the same
default.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Indexing the adjacency word]
\lean{Complexity.adjWord_getD}
\label{Complexity.adjWord_getD}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.getD_flatMap_rows}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $A$ be a Boolean-valued function on pairs of indices in
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $u,v\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. Form a list by concatenating, for
each first index in increasing order, the values of $A$ at that index and all second
indices in increasing order. The entry at zero-based position $un+v$, taking the default
value to be false if the position is out of range, is $A(u,v)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Equality of Two Path Encodings]
\lean{Complexity.PATH_eq_pathRawLang}
\label{Complexity.PATH_eq_pathRawLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.GraphReach, Complexity.PATH, Complexity.adjWord_getD, Complexity.ext_getD', Complexity.length_adjWord, Complexity.pathRawLang, Complexity.rawEdge}
\difficulty{6}
A binary word encodes a reachable directed graph instance using the matrix encoding if
and only if it encodes one using the raw-list encoding. In the matrix encoding, a word
has the form obtained by pairing the unary vertex count, the row-by-row adjacency bits,
and the binary representations of the start and target vertices, with both vertices in
range and the target reachable from the start. In the raw-list encoding, the adjacency
list has exactly $n^2$ bits, both vertices are less than $n$, the word is formed from
the unary count, that list, and the two vertex representations, and the target is
reachable using edges whose corresponding list entries are true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Directed Reachability Lies in NL]
\lean{Complexity.PATH_mem_NL}
\label{Complexity.PATH_mem_NL}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NL, Complexity.PATH, Complexity.PATH_eq_pathRawLang, Complexity.pathRawLang_mem_NL}
\difficulty{1}
The language of encodings of finite directed graphs with a designated start and target
vertex for which the target is reachable from the start belongs to $\mathrm{NL}$. Here
$\mathrm{NL}$ consists of binary languages decidable by a finite nondeterministic Turing
machine using at most a constant multiple of $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$ work-tape cells
on inputs of length $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Completeness of Directed Reachability for NL]
\lean{Complexity.PATH_NLComplete}
\label{Complexity.PATH_NLComplete}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NLComplete, Complexity.PATH, Complexity.PATH_eq_pathRawLang, Complexity.PATH_mem_NL, Complexity.pathRawLang_NLHard}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mathrm{PATH}$ be the language of encodings of finite directed graphs with a
designated start and target vertex for which the target is reachable from the start.
Then $\mathrm{PATH}$ belongs to $\mathrm{NL}$, and every language in $\mathrm{NL}$ has a
log-space many-one reduction to $\mathrm{PATH}$. Here $\mathrm{NL}$ is the class of
binary languages decidable by a finite nondeterministic Turing machine using space
bounded by a constant multiple of $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$.
\end{theorem}
